images.removeDescription: Deletion applies per image ID ({id}), so all tags of this image are removed from this server. Pull it again from the registry if needed.

disk.title: Docker disk
disk.description: {size} used by Docker on this host. The nightly cleanup (04:30) removes old deployments beyond each application's history, unused images, build cache and orphaned registry blobs.
disk.prunable: {count, plural, one {# old deployment will be pruned} other {# old deployments will be pruned}}
disk.orphans: {count, plural, one {# orphan volume} other {# orphan volumes}} (named like aoox's, but no project/application owns it anymore) — only deleted if "Also delete orphan volumes" is checked:
disk.last: Last run {date}: {deployments, plural, one {# deployment} other {# deployments}}, {images, plural, one {# image} other {# images}}, {dangling} dangling, {reclaimed} freed, registry GC {registryGc}, BuildKit cache {buildkit}

confirm.title: Clean up Docker disk now?
confirm.description: Removes old deployments beyond each application's history, unused images and build cache.{registryGc, select, yes { The local registry is garbage-collected too.} other {}}{volumes, plural, =0 {} one { # orphan volume is deleted with its data.} other { # orphan volumes are deleted with their data.}} {containers, plural, =0 {} one {# leftover container is removed.} other {# leftover containers are removed.}} Running applications are not touched. It can take about a minute.

disk.orphanContainers: {count, plural, one {# leftover container} other {# leftover containers}} — left over from projects or apps deleted on older versions; they may still answer on their old domains. Their volumes are not touched.
disk.lastContainers: {count, plural, one {# leftover container removed} other {# leftover containers removed}}

removeContainer.title: Remove this leftover container?
removeContainer.description: {name} belongs to a project or application that no longer exists. It is stopped and removed; its data volumes are kept (see orphan volumes).

disk.orphanComposeVolumes: {count, plural, one {# volume} other {# volumes}} left by deleted stacks (declared inside a compose file). aoox never removes these: check the data is not needed, then remove each one manually on the host.
disk.danglingAnonymous: {count, plural, one {# unused anonymous volume} other {# unused anonymous volumes}} on this Docker host ({size}). Some were left behind by aoox helper containers before they were cleaned up automatically, but Docker does not say who created them, so aoox cannot tell and never removes them. Warning: docker volume prune removes every unused anonymous volume on the host, not just aoox's. List them first and make sure none holds data you need.

ports.infoTitle: ufw does not filter Docker ports
ports.info: Ports that Docker publishes on all interfaces are reachable from the internet even when ufw denies them: Docker adds its own firewall rules that ufw does not manage.
ports.infoFix: Block them in your hosting provider's firewall (security group), or set the port to "This server only" on its resource so it listens on 127.0.0.1.
ports.summary: {open, plural, one {# published port is} other {# published ports are}} open to the internet; {closed} only on this server.
ports.empty: No ports are published on this server.
ports.note: Ports of containers on the host network and ports that are not published do not appear here. The arrow shows the port inside the container.
